newsitem.title: USA: Compromise offered to rescue NJ pension bond plan.
newsitem.headline: Compromise offered to rescue NJ pension bond plan.

text.p: New Jersey legislators Thursday introduced a compromise formulation to rescue Gov. Christie Whitman's plan to sell $2.75 billion in pension bonds.

The bill links the $590 million in budget savings the administration would realize to added state aid to the public schools. The State Supreme Court on May 14 ordered state aid increased by $250 million to 28 local districts it said in 1990 had special needs.
In 1994, the high court ordered the state to equalize per pupil spending in the 28 districts with the average of the state's most affluent districts by September 1997.
The May 14 court order held Whitman to the deadline set in 1994, ruling that her reforms -- setting core curriculum standards -- were helpful but not enough.

Her original pension bond plan was stymied in the state Senate, which whittled it from $3.4 billion to its current size. The new compromise was drafted in the Senate and was introduced by Assemblyman Walter J. Kavanaugh, R-Warren.
It gives state workers a break in pension payments whenever the state uses pension assets to reduce its payments. That would save them a half percent of their salary.
The package has leadership backing, but it's still not clear it will have 21 Republican votes in the state Senate.
